name: gdc-cptac-3
alternateName: CPTAC-Brain, Head and Neck, Kidney, Lung, Pancreas, Uterus
description:
CPTAC-3 is the genomic half of a cohort whose proteomic half lives in a different repository. That split is the single most important practical fact about it: the GDC record carries exome on 1,844 cases, whole genome on 1,827, RNA sequencing on 1,824 and methylation on 1,817, while proteome, phosphoproteome and the scarcer modification layers are distributed through the Proteomic Data Commons under different study identifiers.
Its clinical annotation is unusually strong for a multi-cancer cohort. Vital status is informative for 95.8%, progression or recurrence for 77.9%, and last known disease status for 77.2% - which makes recurrence-based endpoints genuinely available, not just nominally present.
citeAs: Proteogenomic Characterization Reveals Therapeutic Vulnerabilities in Lung Adenocarcinoma

supportedQuestions: Which genomic alterations have consequences at the protein level, and which do not?
What molecular features predict recurrence across cancer types?
Do proteogenomic subtypes cut across tissue of origin?

blockingLimitations.statement: The proteomic data that define this cohort's purpose are not in this record. They are distributed through the Proteomic Data Commons as separate per-fraction studies with their own identifiers, and joining them is the analyst's responsibility.

inappropriateUses: Describing this as a proteogenomic dataset without retrieving the PDC studies.
